title: Preemptive Burst Window Allocator & Isolation Guardrails (Dedicated)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: This PRD describes a combined feature set for Dedicated capacity that provides: a Preemptive Burst Window Allocator (PBWA) which proactively allocates short-lived burst capacity for tenants, and Isolation Guardrails that enforce soft and hard limits to protect other tenants and overall pool SLOs. Goal: increase predictable tail latency for dedicated tenants during transient demand spikes while ensuring fair impact to co-tenants and preserving provider SLAs. Motivation: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect both occasional bursts for traffic spikes and predictable tail latencies. Current behavior allows unbounded soft bursts that can cause noisy neighbor incidents and spikes in p99 latency; operators compensate with conservative overprovisioning. The PBWA aims to reduce unnecessary overprovisioning while providing controlled, measurable burst windows.
background: - Dedicated pools support reserved baseline allocations and loose bursts today. - Observability shows: 40% of burst events last <90s, 22% of tenants account for 70% of cross-tenant p99 spikes, and prewarming is often manual. - Existing features: reservation windows, fairshare policies, predictive autoscale heuristics. Gap: no single mechanism to pre-authorize short bursts with clear accounting and rollback semantics; insufficient guardrails to avoid impacting baseline tenants during widespread spikes.
goals: - Provide a configurable 'burst window' primitive tenants can request (duration, max vGPU/slot count, priority tag). - Implement allocator that preallocates capacity from a burst reservoir or reclaims unused prewarms after window expiry. - Enforce isolation guardrails: soft throttles, priority-based preemption, and minimum baseline protections. - Expose metrics and billing signals for burst consumption. - Ensure graceful fallback to compatible model variants or regions when hard limits hit.
non_goals: - Not a full replacement for long-term autoscale/reservation planning. - Not intended to change per-token pricing model in this iteration. - No changes to on-prem private control plane behavior (VPC will be considered in later roadmap).
requirements:
Functional requirements:
1) API/Console: tenants must be able to request a burst window with parameters {duration_seconds, max_slots, priority_class, allow_preempt} and receive an approved token.
2) Allocation: system must either grant from reserved burst reservoir, temporarily borrow from low-utilized reserved pools, or reject if insufficient.
3) Enforcement: when granted, the tenant may exceed baseline allocation up to max_slots for duration_seconds; system must auto-reclaim or preempt according to priority_class.
4) Failover: on preemption, in-flight requests must either be retried, routed to fallback model variant, or return a clear error with retry-after.
5) Observability: emit events for request/grant/reject/preempt/expire with tenant_id, pool_id, allocation_delta, reason. Dashboard must surface live burst windows and historical consumption by tenant.
6) Billing/Accounting: capture burst usage separately for invoicing and show in Console cost breakdowns.
7) Policy: admins can set per-tenant max concurrent burst windows and pool-level reservoir sizes.
8) Safety: minimum baseline floor per tenant must be honored; eviction must not drop below floor.
9) Autoscale integration: if pool autoscale is active and capacity can be added within latency SLOs, allocator should prefer autoscale vs preempting other tenants.
Non-functional requirements:
A) Grant/Reject decision latency < 200ms for API surface.
B) Provisioning/prewarm latency target < 12s for common model variants.
C) Preemption decision and enforcement within 1s from policy trigger.
D) No measurable increase (>2%) in p99 tail across pool for normal traffic after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end demo: create burst window via API, receive grant token, exercise burst traffic, observe allocation events and cost breakdown entry. 2) Safety: when pool experiences sustained load from other tenants, a granted burst must be preempted according to priority rules and baseline floors preserved. 3) Metrics: measured p50/p95/p99 across pool pre- and post-rollout show <=2% degradation; targeted tenant sees improved p99 during short spikes. 4) Latencies: grant decision <200ms on 95th percentile in staging. 5) Integration tests: simulated concurrent burst requests from 200 tenants across 3 zones; allocator honors global reservoir and per-tenant caps; no pool-level SLA violations. 6) Billing: Console shows separate burst consumption lines and invoices include burst charges in test billing data. 7) Security: audit logs capture every grant/revoke action.
scope:
In-scope:
- API endpoints and Console UI for requesting burst windows and admin reservoir controls.
- Allocation logic (reservoir borrow, low-utilized pull, reject).
- Preemption enforcement and fallback routing to model variant or error.
- Observability events, Console cost visualization, and billing tagging.
- Admin policy controls and per-tenant caps.
Out-of-scope:
- Long-lived reserved allocation marketplace.
- Cross-cloud evacuation and on-prem / air-gapped deployment changes.
- Billing rate redesign (only tagging and visibility included).
design_considerations:
- Preemption model: prefer soft preempt (graceful draining + retry) for allow_preempt=true; hard immediate reclaim only for critical pool health events.
- Priority_class semantics: {P0,P1,P2} where P0 highest and may bypass some soft preempts but counts against 'burst weight' for chargeback.
- Reservoir sizing: default to 10% of pool capacity; adjustable per pool with admin guardrails.
- Fairness: adopt sliding-window consumption accounting to avoid a single tenant monopolizing reservoir.
- Autoscale vs borrow: prefer autoscale when provisioning time and cost thresholds are acceptable; fall back to borrowing when autoscale lag exceeds threshold.
- Safety nets: circuit breaker that globally disables bursts if pool p99 exceeds configured emergency threshold.
metrics:
Primary metrics:
- Tenant burst grant rate, grant rejection rate
- Burst consumption (vGPU-seconds) per tenant and pool
- Pool p50/p95/p99 latency pre/post burst events
- Preemption rate and average reclaim time
- Billing delta attributable to burst usage
SLOs:
- Grant API 95th percentile <200ms
- Preemption enforcement <1s median
- No more than 2% increased p99 for non-bursting tenants after rollout (measured over 30d)
rollout_plan:
1) Canary: internal QA-only pool with small reservoir (5%) and synthetic traffic. Validate grant/revoke flows and billing tags (2 weeks).
2) Beta: invite 5 enterprise customers to opt-in; increase reservoir to 10% in beta pool, monitor for 4 weeks.
3) Gradual ramp: enable for additional pools by 10% of fleet per week with automatic rollback triggers (pool p99 > baseline + 3% or preemption > threshold).
4) GA: enable self-serve in Console with admin policy defaults.
Rollback criteria:
- Pool-level p99 > baseline + 3% sustained for 30m.
- Preemption failures > 0.5% of preemption attempts over 1h.
- Billing/chargeback inconsistencies identified in staging.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator decision matrix (reservoir vs borrow vs reject).
- Integration tests: API grant -> provisioning -> traffic generation -> revoke -> fallback.
- Chaos tests: simulate node failures and ensure reservoir accounting remains consistent.
- Load tests: hundreds of concurrent burst requests across pools to validate fairness and performance.
- Billing validation: synthetic invoices to confirm burst tagging flows to billing pipeline.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: noisy neighbor preemption could be insufficient and degrade baseline tenants. Mitigation: strict minimum baseline floors, emergency circuit breaker, and conservative default reservoir.
Risk: inaccurate billing leading to revenue leakage. Mitigation: end-to-end billing tests and invoice reconciliation during beta.
Risk: allocation decision complexity causing latency. Mitigation: cache hot policy decisions and design decision path for O(1) checks for common cases.
Risk: customer confusion about burst pricing. Mitigation: clear Console copy, examples, and automated billing preview during request flow.
open_questions:
- What default reservoir percentage should be used per pool for different pool sizes?
- Should burst pricing be a linear multiplier or tiered? (billing team decision)
- What's the correct UX to explain preemption order to customers?
- How to expose fallback model variant mappings in the Console?
notes: Implementation should prioritize clean observability hooks so SRE and support can diagnose incidents. Schedule a cross-functional design review in Cycle 2026-W12. Follow-on work: extend PBWA to Private deployments and add marketplace for paid burst credits.
public_release_notes: Introducing Burst Windows for Dedicated capacity: short-lived, admin-controlled burst allocations with transparent billing and automatic guardrails to protect baseline SLAs. Initially opt-in via Beta, GA later in 2026.
